## The idea

The last two chords can make an eight-bar phrase stop, pause, or turn away from
an expected destination. Hold the preceding material steady and the distinction
becomes plain. V to I reaches home with pressure behind it. IV to I arrives more
gently. A phrase that ends on V remains open, while V to vi aims toward tonic
and changes course at the last moment.

A *cadence* is a conventional harmonic gesture at a phrase boundary. Those four
behaviours are called authentic, plagal, half, and deceptive cadences. Learn the
names alongside the sounds they organise. A cadence is not merely a two-chord
arrow on a page; it describes how that arrow behaves after enough context has
made a boundary audible.

## Run this

```{.ruby audio=""}
use_bpm 88
use_synth :piano

chords = {
  I: chord(:c4, :major).to_a,
  IV: chord(:f3, :major).to_a,
  V: chord(:g3, :major).to_a,
  vi: chord(:a3, :minor).to_a
}

define :play_cadence_phrase do |chords, ending|
  body = [:I, :vi, :IV, :V, :I, :IV]
  (body + ending).each do |name|
    play_chord chords[name], release: 1.7
    sleep 2
  end
end

endings = {
  authentic: [:V, :I],
  plagal: [:IV, :I],
  half: [:IV, :V],
  deceptive: [:V, :vi]
}

endings.each do |name, ending|
  puts name
  play_cadence_phrase chords, ending
  sleep 2
end
```

The common six-chord body gives each ending something to punctuate. Both
authentic and plagal cadences reach I, but V carries the leading tone and creates
stronger forward pressure than IV. The half cadence stops at that pressure point.
The deceptive ending moves to vi instead; because I and vi share two tones, the
substitution sounds connected even as the expected destination slips away.

## Change one thing

1. Remove the shared body and play each ending by itself. The chord pairs remain
   different, but their cadential identities weaken because there is less phrase
   motion for them to complete or interrupt.
2. Hold the final chord for four beats. Extra duration gives every boundary more
   authority, though it cannot supply the tonic missing from a half cadence.
3. Put E in the bass of the final I. The authentic labels remain V-I, yet the
   inverted tonic carries less weight at the bottom and softens the landing.

## Why it works

V contains B, one semitone below C. Add F to make V7 and two active tones appear:
B tends upward to C while F tends downward to E. IV approaches tonic through a
different pair of short motions, F to E and A to G, without the dominant's
leading-tone pressure. Both cadences use economical voice movement, but the
approach harmony prepares a different kind of arrival.

A half cadence stops after the directional harmony has been stated. V can
support a pause, but it still predicts continuation. The deceptive cadence uses
that prediction against the listener. Instead of the expected C-E-G, it gives
A-C-E. Two tonic tones arrive as promised while a new bass reinterprets them as
vi.

The program represents each cadence as a two-symbol suffix appended to common
body data. That makes the comparison honest: only the ending varies. The
renderer has no special instruction to sound conclusive or deceptive. It plays
the named chords, and their order acquires meaning within the tonal context
established beforehand.

Melody can reinforce or resist the harmonic boundary. A final C over tonic
aligns bass, harmony, and melodic goal. An E allows the harmony to close while
the upper voice sounds less rooted; G retains more openness still. Cadence names
therefore describe a harmonic skeleton, not every detail a listener hears at
the end of the phrase.

Timing changes the result too. Silence after V can let a half cadence register
as a deliberate question. Moving immediately into the next phrase turns the
same chord into a connector. Keep pauses and durations fixed for the four-way
comparison, then vary them once the harmonic difference is clear enough that a
timing cue will not be mistaken for a new cadence type.

## Take it further

Create a ten-trial drill from the four endings. Begin with `use_random_seed 42`,
choose one ending, play the common body and cadence, leave four beats for an
answer, and then print its name. Keep voicing, duration, synth, and pause length
constant. Record confusions by pair, especially authentic versus plagal and half
versus deceptive; those errors tell you which kind of boundary needs a slower
comparison.
